answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a costly, verifiable stake instead of a free signup: an agent must lock a deposit of quartz-backed value, or burn timber-priced compute, before its reputation counts. Peers then grade work through a trellis of mutual attestations — an agent's standing grows only through verified interactions with already-staked agents, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs more than any reward they could extract, and bad actors are pruned before they drain the pool.
